item.title: windmill-labs/windmill
item.description:
Code-first platform for workflows, apps and AI agents, on the fastest self-hostable orchestrator (benchmarked against Airflow, Prefect and Temporal). Business teams build with AI, engineers control what ships. Open-source alternative to Lovable, Retool and n8n.

https://windmill.dev

Open-source, self-hostable code-first platform for workflows, apps and AI agents, running on the fastest self-hostable orchestrator. Engineers write code in 20+ languages and sync it with Git. Business teams build on the same platform with AI, while review, promotion between environments and isolated workers keep engineers in control of what ships. Self-hostable alternative to Lovable, Retool, n8n and a simplified Temporal.

Scripts are turned into sharable UIs, APIs and cron jobs automatically, and can be composed together into flows, data pipelines, AI agents or full-code React and Svelte apps. Supported languages: Python, TypeScript, Go, Bash, SQL, GraphQL, PowerShell, Rust, and more.

Try it - Website - Docs - Discord - Hub - Contributing

Windmill - Code-first platform for workflows, apps and AI agents

Windmill is fully open-sourced (AGPLv3) and Windmill Labs offers dedicated instances and commercial support and licenses.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d80de1d9-64de-4d89-aacd-6df23fa81fc4

  • Windmill - Code-first platform for workflows, apps and AI agents
    • Build with AI, ship with review
    • Main Concepts
    • What the code looks like
    • Data: data tables, DuckDB and DuckLake
    • Develop locally or in the browser
    • Stack
    • Fastest Self-Hostable Workflow Engine
    • Security
    • Performance
    • Architecture
    • How to self-host
      • Docker compose
      • Kubernetes (Helm charts)
      • Cloud providers
      • OAuth, SSO & SMTP
      • License
      • Integrations
    • Environment Variables
    • Contributing
    • Copyright

Build with AI, ship with review

Business teams and engineers build on the same Windmill instance. What the AI builds is an ordinary script, flow or app, and goes through the same review as code written by engineers:

  • AI sessions build scripts, flows and apps with AI in a workspace fork, with a live preview and a diff to review before deploying.
  • Workspace roles decide what each team can author, and folders scope the resources, skills and MCP servers its AI can reach.
  • Protection rulesets block direct deployment, so changes reach production only after an engineer reviews and deploys them.
  • Dev workspaces keep their own credentials, and promote to prod through Compare & Deploy or a Git pull request.
  • Worker groups run AI-built code on its own workers, or on a separate instance.

See let business teams build with AI safely for the full setup. Engineers keep writing code locally with the CLI, the VS Code extension and their coding agent, synced with Git.

Main Concepts

  1. Define a minimal and generic script in Python, TypeScript, Go or Bash that solves a specific task. The code can be defined in the provided Web IDE or synchronized with your own GitHub repo (e.g. through VS Code extension): provided Web IDE or synchronized with your own GitHub repo (e.g. through VS Code extension):

  1. Your scripts parameters are automatically parsed and generate a frontend.

  1. Make it flow! You can chain your scripts or scripts made by the community shared on WindmillHub.

  1. Build complex UIs on top of your scripts and flows.

Scripts and flows can be triggered by schedules, webhooks, HTTP routes, Kafka, WebSockets, emails, and more.

Build your entire infra on top of Windmill!

What the code looks like

A script is a plain function. Its typed arguments become a generated form, an HTTP endpoint and a CLI command:

import * as wmill from "windmill-client";
import dayjs from "dayjs"; // any npm package, resolved and pinned automatically

export async function main(
  customerId: string,
  plan: "starter" | "pro", // a union of strings becomes a dropdown
  trialDays = 14 // defaults infer the type
) {
  const trialEnd = dayjs().add(trialDays, "day").toISOString();

  // a data table: the workspace's Postgres, queried without a connection string
  const sql = wmill.datatable();
  await sql`INSERT INTO trials (customer_id, plan, trial_end) VALUES (${customerId}, ${plan}, ${trialEnd})`.fetch();

  // secrets are permissioned by path
  const slackToken = await wmill.getVariable("f/sales/slack_token");
  await fetch("https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${slackToken}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ channel: "#sales", text: `New ${plan} trial: ${customerId}` }),
  });

  console.log(`Trial started for ${customerId}`); // logs stream live in the UI
  return { customerId, plan, trialEnd }; // returned as JSON
}

Workflows are code too. Each task runs as its own job with its own logs, and waiting for an approval releases the worker:

import { task, waitForApproval, workflow } from "windmill-client";

async function plan(env: string) {
  return { env, changes: 3 };
}

async function apply(plan: { env: string; changes: number }) {
  return `applied ${plan.changes} changes to ${plan.env}`;
}

export const main = workflow(async (env: string) => {
  const changes = await task(plan)(env);
  const approval = await waitForApproval({ timeout: 3600 });
  if (!approval.approved) {
    return `rejected by ${approval.approver}`;
  }
  return await task(apply)(changes);
});

Flows can also be built in the visual flow editor or as YAML, with scripts like the first one as steps. See workflows as code.

Data: data tables, DuckDB and DuckLake

  • Data tables give each workspace managed Postgres tables, queried with type-checked SQL from TypeScript, Python and DuckDB scripts without exposing a connection string.
  • DuckDB scripts query S3 and Azure Blob files (CSV, Parquet, JSON), data tables, Postgres, MySQL and BigQuery in SQL, on your workers.
  • DuckLake stores large datasets as lakehouse tables in your workspace object storage, queried in plain SQL.
  • Pipelines (alpha) wire scripts by the data they read and write instead of a hand-drawn DAG. This script runs whenever events is materialized, and materializes its own table:
-- pipeline
-- on ducklake://main/events
-- materialize ducklake://main/events_by_kind
ATTACH 'ducklake://main' AS dl;
SELECT kind, count(*) AS n
FROM dl.events
GROUP BY kind;

Existing dbt projects run unmodified as scripts. See the pipelines quickstart.

Develop locally or in the browser

Engineers work from their editor and coding agent, business teams build with AI in the browser, and both land in the same workspace:

Tool Description
CLI Sync a workspace with local files and Git, run scripts and flows from the command line. wmill init generates AGENTS.md and skill files for Claude Code, Cursor and other AI tools
VS Code extension Edit and test scripts and flows from VS Code or Cursor with full IDE support
Git sync Two-way sync between a workspace and your Git repository
MCP server Let coding agents and AI clients run scripts, manage resources and monitor jobs in a workspace
AI sessions The same agent loop in the browser, with nothing to install: plan mode, skills and MCP servers, a live preview, and a diff to review before deploying, in a fork of the workspace

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c541c326-e9ae-4602-a09a-1989aaded1e9

You can run scripts locally by passing the right environment variables for the wmill client library to fetch resources and variables from your instance. See local development docs.

Stack

  • Database: Postgres (compatible with Aurora, Cloud SQL, Neon, Azure PostgreSQL)
  • Backend: Rust - stateless API servers and workers pulling jobs from a Postgres queue
  • Frontend: Svelte 5
  • Sandboxing: nsjail and PID namespace isolation
  • Runtimes:
    • TypeScript/JavaScript: Bun (default); Deno only on the windmill-full images
    • Python: python3 with uv for dependency management
    • PHP: only on the windmill-full images
    • Go, Bash, PowerShell, Rust, C#, Java, Ansible

Fastest Self-Hostable Workflow Engine

We have compared Windmill to other self-hostable workflow engines (Airflow, Prefect & Temporal) and Windmill is the most performant solution for both benchmarks: one flow composed of 40 lightweight tasks & one flow composed of 10 long-running tasks.

All methodology & results on our Benchmarks page.

Security

  • Sandboxing: nsjail for filesystem/resource isolation, and PID namespace isolation (enabled by default) to prevent jobs from accessing worker process memory
  • Secrets: One encryption key per workspace for credentials stored in Windmill's K/V store. We recommend encrypting the Postgres database as well.

See Security documentation for details.

Performance

Once a job started, there is no overhead compared to running the same script on the node with its corresponding runner (Deno/Go/Python/Bash). The added latency from a job being pulled from the queue, started, and then having its result sent back to the database is ~50ms. A typical lightweight deno job will take around 100ms total.

Architecture

Stateless API servers and workers share a PostgreSQL database that holds the job queue and all workspace state (remote agent workers go through the API servers instead). Workers pull jobs by tag, so each worker group can run in its own network, for example dev workers that only reach dev systems and prod workers that only run reviewed code.

How to self-host

For detailed setup options, see Self-Host documentation.

Docker compose

Deploy Windmill with 3 files (docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile, .env):

curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/windmill-labs/windmill/main/docker-compose.yml -o docker-compose.yml
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/windmill-labs/windmill/main/Caddyfile -o Caddyfile
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/windmill-labs/windmill/main/.env -o .env

docker compose up -d

Go to http://localhost - default credentials: admin@windmill.dev / changeme

Using an external database: Set DATABASE_URL in .env to point to your managed Postgres (AWS RDS, GCP Cloud SQL, Azure, Neon, etc.) and set db replicas to 0.

Kubernetes (Helm charts)

helm repo add windmill https://windmill-labs.github.io/windmill-helm-charts/
helm install windmill-chart windmill/windmill --namespace=windmill --create-namespace

See windmill-helm-charts for configuration options.

Cloud providers

Windmill works on AWS (EKS/ECS), GCP, Azure, Ubicloud, Fly.io, Render.com, Hetzner, Digital Ocean, and others. Rule of thumb: 1 worker per 1vCPU and 1-2 GB RAM.

OAuth, SSO & SMTP

Configure OAuth and SSO (Google Workspace, Microsoft/Azure, Okta) directly from the superadmin UI. See documentation.

License

  • Using the Community Edition as is, internally or through its APIs, is free and needs no commercial license, within the limits and quotas set in the software.
  • Selling, reselling or serving the Community Edition as a managed service, modifying or wrapping it, or re-exposing it to your users as a feature of your product (iframed public apps excepted) requires a commercial license: contact sales@windmill.dev.
  • The binary built from this repository without the enterprise feature flag is open source under AGPLv3: the same uses are then allowed under the AGPLv3 terms, or with a commercial license. The API clients and the OpenAPI spec are Apache 2.0.

See LICENSE for the full terms and Pricing for plans.

Integrations

In Windmill, integrations are referred to as resources and resource types. Each Resource has a Resource Type that defines the schema that the resource needs to implement.

On self-hosted instances, you might want to import all the approved resource types from WindmillHub. A setup script will prompt you to have it being synced automatically everyday.

Environment Variables

The variables most deployments set:

Environment Variable name Default Description Api Server/Worker/All
DATABASE_URL The Postgres database url. All
MODE standalone The mode of the binary: standalone, server, worker, agent (EE), indexer (EE image, full-text search), mcp All
WORKER_GROUP default The worker group the worker belongs to and gets its configuration pulled from Worker
BASE_URL http://localhost:8000 The base url that is exposed publicly to access your instance. Is overriden by the instance settings if any. Server
LICENSE_KEY (EE only) None License key checked at startup for the Enterprise Edition of Windmill Worker

All other variables (database pool, queue, runtimes, private registries, certificates, zombie jobs and more) are documented in the environment variables reference.

Contributing

At this time, we are not seeking outside contribution. Bug reports and feature requests remain very welcome, and small, trivially-verified PRs that fix a problem are still accepted. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full policy.

To run Windmill from source, see frontend/README_DEV.md.

item.title: tw93/Pake
item.description:
Turn any website into a lightweight desktop app with one command, on macOS, Windows and Linux.

https://pake.run

Pake

Turn any website into a lightweight desktop app with one command. Supports macOS, Windows and Linux. Free open-source CLI, plus a desktop app.

English · 中文 · 繁體 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Deutsch · Français

This repo is the free open-source Pake CLI, and everything below stays free. Prefer a graphical app? The Pake desktop app is a separate download from pake.run, its only official site. It makes apps from a ready-made gallery or any URL without Node.js or Rust, with settings, updates and separate apps for other accounts in one window. pnpm install -g pake-cli installs the CLI only.

Features

  • Lightweight: Installers are typically under 10 MB, nearly 20 times smaller than Electron packages, a lighter alternative to Nativefier and other Electron wrappers
  • Fast: Built with Rust Tauri on the system WebView instead of a bundled Chromium, so each app carries no browser engine of its own
  • Easy to use: One-command packaging via CLI or online building, no complex configuration needed
  • Feature-rich: Supports shortcuts, immersive windows, drag & drop, style customization, ad removal

Getting Started

  • Beginners: Make apps without a command line in the Pake desktop app, download ready-made Popular Packages or use Online Building with no environment setup required
  • Developers: Install CLI Tool for one-command packaging of any website with customizable icons, window settings, and more
  • Advanced Users: Clone the project locally for Custom Development, or check Advanced Usage for style customization and feature enhancement
  • Troubleshooting: Check FAQ for common issues and solutions

Popular Packages

WeRead Mac Windows Linux X Mac Windows Linux
Grok Mac Windows Linux DeepSeek Mac Windows Linux
ChatGPT Mac Windows Linux Gemini Mac Windows Linux
YouTube Music Mac Windows Linux YouTube Mac Windows Linux
LiZhi Mac Windows Linux ProgramMusic Mac Windows Linux
Excalidraw Mac Windows Linux XiaoHongShu Mac Windows Linux
Notion Mac Windows Linux Flomo Mac Windows Linux

More apps are on the Releases page.

Keyboard shortcuts
Mac Windows/Linux Function
⌘ + [ Ctrl + [ Return to the previous page
⌘ + ] Ctrl + ] Go to the next page
⌘ + ↑ Ctrl + ↑ Auto scroll to top of page
⌘ + ↓ Ctrl + ↓ Auto scroll to bottom of page
⌘ + R Ctrl + R Refresh page
⌘ + W Ctrl + W Hide window, not quit
⌘ + - Ctrl + - Zoom out
⌘ + = Ctrl + = Zoom in
⌘ + 0 Ctrl + 0 Reset zoom
⌘ + L Ctrl + L Copy current page URL
⌘ + ⇧ + ⌥ + V Ctrl + Shift + V Paste and match style
⌘ + ⇧ + H Ctrl + Shift + H Go to home page
⌘ + ⌥ + I Ctrl + Shift + I Toggle developer tools (debug only)
⌘ + ⇧ + ⌫ Ctrl + Shift + Del Clear cache and restart
⌃ + ⌘ + F F11 Toggle native window fullscreen

Double-click the title bar to toggle fullscreen. On Windows and Linux, --hide-window-decorations gives a frameless window with a top drag region. On Mac, swipe to go back or forward and drag the title bar to move the window, and the menu bar has navigation, zoom and window controls.

Command-Line Packaging

# Install Pake CLI
pnpm install -g pake-cli

# Basic usage, fetches the website icon automatically
pake https://github.com --name GitHub

# Advanced usage, custom options
pake https://weekly.tw93.fun --name Weekly --icon https://cdn.tw93.fun/pake/weekly.icns --width 1200 --height 800 --hide-title-bar

The first build sets up the environment and takes a while, later builds are fast. See the CLI Usage Guide for every option, or try GitHub Actions Online Building if you'd rather skip the command line.

Using Pake from a script or AI agent? Pass --json for machine-readable results, describe apps declaratively with --config app.json (schema), and package local build output directly with pake ./dist --name MyTool. See llms.txt for the full agent contract. The official skill installs like this:

# Claude Code
/plugin marketplace add tw93/Pake
/plugin install pake@pake

# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add tw93/Pake
codex plugin add pake@pake

Copy this to your AI agent to get started:

Use Pake (npm i -g pake-cli) to package webpages as desktop apps. Read https://unpkg.com/pake-cli@latest/llms.txt first; always run pake with --json and parse stdout as a single JSON object. Package <url-or-local-dist> into an app named <AppName>.

Development

Requires Rust >=1.85 and Node >=22 (recommended LTS; >=20.9 also works), see the Tauri documentation for setup. If you are new to this toolchain, the CLI is the easier path.

# Install dependencies
pnpm i

# Local development, right-click to open the debug tools
pnpm run dev

# Build application
pnpm run build

For style customization, feature enhancement, container communication and other advanced features, see Advanced Usage Documentation.

Contributors

Pake wouldn't be possible without these incredible contributors.

Support

  • Getting the Pake desktop app is the most direct way to support Pake's development
  • If Pake helped you, give it a star, share it, or open an issue or PR, including sites that would make good desktop apps
  • I have two cats, TangYuan and Coke, and if Pake makes your life a little easier, feel free to treat them to canned food

These lovely people already did

License

Pake is open source under GPL-3.0, see LICENSE and Pake Output Exception; apps you build with Pake are entirely yours to use and distribute. If you fork Pake into your own product, to avoid confusion please give it a different name and credit Pake as the source. Pake CLI stays open source for the long run.
